# RIVER COMMONS

## Site
- Project: waterfront public library and summer refuge.
- Site identity: site-overhead.png.
- Boundary and surrounding geometry: site-plan.png, boundary A–D.
- Design area: approximately 4,563 m².
- Recorded boundary lengths: approximately 24 / 147 / 39 / 145 m.
- Existing site elements: levee, railway, railway retaining wall and river edge.
- Source and datum record: source-status.md.
- Vertical reference: local ±0.000, as recorded in source-status.md.
- Riverbank sampled level: −1.10 m.
- Railway embankment sampled level: +4.48 m.
- Project flood scenario: +3.5 m.

## Building geometry
- Ground level: open undercroft at ±0.000.
- Ground-level overhead clearance: 4.5 m.
- Level 1 finished floor: +4.80 m.
- Level 2 finished floor: +9.30 m.
- Roof level: +13.80 m.
- Enclosed gross floor area: 6,800 m².
- Level 1 gross floor area: 3,400 m².
- Level 2 gross floor area: 3,400 m².
- Ground undercroft: outside the enclosed gross floor area total.
- Net accommodation: 2,800 m² per occupied floor.
- Circulation, cores, partitions and structure allowance: 600 m² per occupied floor.
- Waterfront route clear width: 4 m.
- South- and west-facing occupied-room glazing: external shading projection 2 m.
- Public vertical circulation: one passenger lift and two stairs connecting the ground level and both occupied floors.

## Operations

- Public Support contents: toilets, drinking-water point, cleaner's room and storage.
- Public route: street, public entrance, occupied floors and waterfront.
- Service route: separate delivery and staff access.

# TIDELINE LIBRARY — real site, historical baseline and client scenario

The supplied inputs are site-overhead.png (a real, locked 2019 orthorectified aerial with a marked design extent) and site-plan.png (a deterministic plan of the same extent and selected existing context), plus this text. Both boards use boundary A–D, grid north and metric scale. No existing library or proposed scheme is shown. The tested system receives the two PNG boards and this text.

## Actual site and source limits

The setting is a grass strip on the landward side of the Ohio River flood barrier at Cairo, Illinois, USA. The approximately 4,563 m² quadrilateral is an author-defined design extent inside the visible grass, not a cadastral parcel or assertion of ownership. It is approximately 145 m long and 24–39 m wide, with A–B / B–C / C–D / D–A sides of approximately 24 / 147 / 39 / 145 m. The 6,800 m² in the brief is proposed total gross floor area across floors and phases, not site area.

From west to east the existing relationship is: neighbourhood and city street; grass design extent; flood barrier; elevated railway corridor; riverbank; Ohio River. The railway is not a public promenade. Preserve the external flood barrier, railway, streets and adjoining properties. The commissioned levee-side public walk is a proposed landward interface within the design extent; orient the main entrance to it and connect it to the city sidewalk. No existing pedestrian crossing of the barrier or tracks is assumed. The public walk is a design requirement, not a feature claimed to exist in the aerial.

Plan alignments and the author boundary were digitised from the 2019 aerial with an estimated tracing uncertainty of about 2 m, not survey-certified accuracy. Two selected neighbouring roof outlines are shown; blank areas do not imply vacant land. See the real aerial for complete visible context. Gray road bands and line weights indicate corridors, not measured widths. Heights of neighbouring buildings, floodwall crest height and exact track/road widths are not established. The blank triangle over the far river is NoData outside the selected 2019 image footprint, not dry land. It has not been filled with AI or a different year's image.

## One explicit vertical datum

The real terrain source is a 1 m USGS 3DEP bare-earth DEM, acquired in 2020 and published in 2022, with heights in metres NAVD88. The aerial is from 2019; these are different historical acquisitions, not one current survey. Local zero for this design exercise is defined at UTM zone 16N easting 306545.847 m, northing 4098094.268 m: 0.00 m local = approximately 94.81 m NAVD88 (recorded DEM sample 94.808303833 m).

Approximate DEM samples, all relative to this same local zero: A −0.16 m, B +0.15 m, C +0.37 m, D −0.15 m; nearby city street −0.37 m; railway embankment +4.48 m; riverbank −1.10 m. These are conceptual terrain references from a 1 m raster, not surveyed point levels. The railway sample is ground/embankment, not a railway clearance or public-walk level. Bare-earth DEM does not establish a thin wall's crest. A water-pixel terrain value is not a measured river level and is not supplied as one.

## Client design requirements and assumptions

- Design flood level: **+3.5 m** in the above local datum (arithmetically about 98.31 m NAVD88). This is an author-defined client scenario, not an official flood level, FEMA base flood elevation, historical high-water mark, tide statistic or regulatory requirement.
- Put habitable floor area above that client flood level. Raise the occupied ground floor and retain **4.5 m** clear height beneath it for an open floodable undercroft. Clear height is the physical distance between proposed ground and the underside of the raised floor; it is not an absolute elevation. Label both the datum-based floor/flood elevations and this clear dimension in the key section.
- Flood protection governs if it conflicts with public access. Work within the marked extent and preserve the barrier and railway. The accessible landward walk/entrance connection is designed without assuming permission to cut through those features.
- Total gross floor area is **6,800 m²**, capable of phased delivery. Combine community reading, a stepped reading hall and evening public life.

No tide regime is asserted for this inland river site. No current legal approval, flood certification, ownership or construction readiness is implied by this design brief.

## Sources and reuse

- [USGS National Map NAIP imagery service](https://imagery.nationalmap.gov/arcgis/rest/services/USGSNAIPImagery/ImageServer): USDA NAIP 0.6 m natural-colour imagery, locked raster 53773, image m_3708963_se_16_060_20190912, acquired 2019-09-12. The board uses a 0.5 m export in EPSG:32616; resampling does not improve source resolution or establish accuracy. The dedicated NAIP service states public-domain use. No commercial NAIP Plus imagery is used.
- [USGS 3DEP elevation service](https://elevation.nationalmap.gov/arcgis/rest/services/3DEPElevation/ImageServer): raster 63818, project IL_HicksDome_FluorsparDistrict_2019_D19; despite the project name, source metadata lists 2020 acquisition and 2022 publication. [USGS 3DEP products](https://www.usgs.gov/3d-elevation-program) are available without use restrictions.
- [USACE National Levee Database system 4005000001](https://levees.sec.usace.army.mil/levees/4005000001) supports the Cairo flood-defence context; it does not supply the client-specified design flood scenario or a surveyed wall-crest level here.

Credit: USDA NAIP / USGS National Map; USGS 3DEP. Downloaded 2026-09-06. Source requests, raw crop, DEM samples and author geometry are retained for author-side reproduction, not issued as additional benchmark inputs. This is a source-based design exercise; no government endorsement is claimed.

steps.userMessage:
RIVER COMMONS | Waterfront public library and summer refuge

We are commissioning a public library and summer refuge within boundary A–D on the attached waterfront site. The design area is approximately 4,563 m², with recorded boundary lengths of approximately 24 / 147 / 39 / 145 m. The existing levee, railway and river edge establish the setting. Give residents a legible route between the street, library and waterfront, with separate access for deliveries and staff.

The building has an open ground level and two enclosed public floors of 3,400 m² each, totaling 6,800 m². Use the local datum ±0.000 recorded in source-status.md: the riverbank sample is −1.10 m, the railway embankment sample is +4.48 m and the project flood scenario is +3.5 m. Ground-level overhead clearance is 4.5 m; occupied floor levels are +4.80 m and +9.30 m, with the roof at +13.80 m. Provide a continuous 4 m clear waterfront route and step-free access to both occupied floors. The room schedule in 01-client-facts.en.md allocates 2,800 m² net accommodation to each floor. Use concrete supports, cross-laminated timber floors and exposed glulam beams in the Cooling Commons and Reading Room.

Summer refuge operates from June 1 to October 15, daily from 10:00 to 18:00, with 80 seats in the Cooling Commons. The Community Room accommodates 80 people from 18:00 to 21:00 through its own entrance and toilet access while the reading areas close. Print "RIVER COMMONS" at the public entrance and on drawing titles; print "Cooling Commons" on that room's entrance sign and plan label.

Audience: surrounding residents, library staff and the municipal project team, for choosing the building arrangement and agreeing how reading, summer refuge and evening activities share the site.

Inputs (attached): 01-client-facts.en.md contains the dimensions, room areas, operating hours and material requirements. 02-delivery-catalog.en.md lists the deliverables, proportions, formats and stages. site-overhead.png is the identity source for the existing waterfront setting. site-plan.png is the constraint image for boundary A–D, north, scale and surrounding connections. source-status.md records the aerial's date and source, the vertical datum, sampled levels and the project flood scenario.

Deliverables:
1. Three distinct architectural direction boards, each with site organization, massing and public circulation
2. Two written specification documents: a selection and ten-room schedule with direction number, IDs, names, net areas, clear heights, adjacencies and floor levels; and a materials and construction schedule with elements, materials, assemblies and exposure
3. One selected-scheme site plan with boundary A–D, waterfront route and public and service connections
4. Three floor-plan sheets: one coordinated ground-and-occupied-floor overview repeating the room schedule's names, areas and levels, one enlarged Cooling Commons plan and one enlarged Community Room evening plan
5. Three section sheets: the levee–railway–building–river section, an enlarged Cooling Commons section and an enlarged Reading Room section
6. Two elevation sheets: all four building faces and an enlarged waterfront elevation with shading and material junctions
7. Two shading and spatial strategy sheets: an overview with room depths, opening locations and areas; and south- and west-facing shading assembly details
8. Six eye-level public views: daytime Cooling Commons, evening Community Room, waterfront approach, Reading Room, Children's Library and evening arrival
9. One 12-second spatial walkthrough connecting the waterfront approach, Cooling Commons and Community Room
10. One presentation of at least twelve pages, reusing the directions, selection, both schedules, drawings and six public views

Acceptance:
- The three direction boards precede the selection and room schedule; both specification documents and every subsequent drawing, view, video and presentation develop its named selection. The presentation's first page repeats the direction number and its schedule pages repeat all ten room IDs, names, areas and levels.
- The floor-plan overview totals 3,400 m² gross per occupied floor and locates every room from the room schedule, one lift and two stairs. The two enlarged plans repeat their parent plan's room boundaries, entrances, IDs, names and areas; the site plan retains A–D and existing levee and railway positions, with a dimensioned 4 m waterfront route and separate service access. Site and floor plans carry north arrows and metric scale bars.
- The site-and-building section labels ±0.000, −1.10 m, +4.48 m, +3.5 m, +4.80 m, +9.30 m and +13.80 m and dimensions 4.5 m ground clearance. The enlarged room sections repeat their scheduled 3.6 m clear heights and floor levels, with room depths matching the enlarged plans or floor-plan overview.
- Both strategy sheets and the waterfront elevation show 2 m south- and west-facing shading projections. The strategy overview lists Cooling Commons and Reading Room opening areas; the materials schedule, enlarged sections, shading details and presentation repeat the concrete supports, cross-laminated timber floors, exposed glulam beams and aluminum shading assemblies.
- The Cooling Commons plan and daytime view show 80 seats; the Community Room plan and evening view show 80 places. The evening plan and arrival view share the same independent access and reading-area closure line. The presentation states June 1–October 15, daytime 10:00–18:00 and evening 18:00–21:00 alongside these operating arrangements.
- All six public views and the 12-second video match the plans, sections and elevations in columns, openings, levels and material zones, with the existing waterfront identifiable from site-overhead.png. Drawing titles, entrance elevations and presentation carry RIVER COMMONS; the daytime view shows the Cooling Commons entrance sign, and the presentation reuses both schedules and all six views across at least twelve pages.

Please clearly mark which version you consider the final deliverable. If nothing is marked, the last exported version counts.
